purpose: Nelfinavir is used to treat HIV infection, the virus that can lead to AIDS. It is always used in combination with other HIV medicines, never alone. It helps keep the amount of HIV virus in your body as low as possible so your immune system can stay stronger.
how_it_works: HIV needs a special tool called a protease enzyme to make copies of itself inside your body. Nelfinavir blocks that tool, so the virus cannot make new, working copies of itself. This slows down the spread of HIV in your body and helps protect your immune system.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is diarrhea, which affects many people taking this medicine. You may also experience nausea, gas, or an upset stomach. Some people notice skin rash or feel more tired than usual.
warnings: Tell your doctor about all medicines you take because nelfinavir interacts with many drugs, including some common ones. Do not take it with certain heart rhythm medicines, sedatives like triazolam or midazolam, or the migraine drug ergotamine, as this can cause dangerous reactions. If you have liver problems, let your doctor know. Women taking birth control pills should use a backup method, because nelfinavir can make the pill less effective. Never stop taking your HIV medicines without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1,250 mg (five 250 mg tablets) taken twice a day, or 750 mg three times a day. It should always be taken with a meal or snack to help your body absorb it properly. Your doctor will decide the best dose and schedule for you.
